newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH VENTURE CAPITAL FIRM ALPINVEST TO BE FLOATED.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH VENTURE CAPITAL FIRM ALPINVEST TO BE FLOATED.

text.p: Shares in Dutch venture capital firm Alpinvest will be floated on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in the first half of this year, the Dutch Economic Affairs Ministry said on Friday.
"The State ... intends to sell its complete shareholding of 30,3 percent and ABN AMRO Bank , currently a 48,5 percent shareholder, a large share of its holding," the ministry said in a statement.
It added that ABN AMRO Rothschild had been appointed as lead-manager and bookrunner on the sale of Alpinvest shares. Barclays de Zoete Wedd was appointed as senior co-lead manager.
The other syndicate members will be appointed later.
The ministry said the Alpinvest shares would be sold through an initial public offering.

Alpinvest has repeatedly said it intended to seek a bourse listing and the Dutch government announced last July it had appointed investment bank NatWest Markets as its financial advisor on the sale of its Alpinvest stake.

Alpinvest posted 1996 first-half net profits of 55.3 million guilders, down from 65.6 million in the year-earlier period, and said in August it expected full-year net to be slightly below 1995's 71 million guilders.
